title: Localization string table
description: Source of truth for every player-visible string in a game. One entry per key with every language beside it. loc.py validates every document against THIS FILE first (shape: types, enums, patterns, caps), then applies the checks a document grammar cannot express: placeholder parity across languages, arg declaration/use parity, the plural categories each language's rule can actually select, fallback completeness, and C identifier collisions. loc_test.py's SchemaIsLoadBearing pins every value that appears on both sides, so the two cannot drift apart.

languages.description: Every language the table carries. Key order fixes the generated LocLang enum order, so it is append-only in practice.

group_separator.description: Inserted every three digits by the int:group arg type. Russian uses a space, English a comma. Digit grouping is language data, not game code.

group_min_digits.description: Grouping applies only once the integer part has at least this many digits. Russian typography groups from five, English from four.

alphabet.description: Every letter this language can write, whether or not the corpus uses it today. Optional. The generated font charset is otherwise exactly the characters the corpus happens to contain, which is correct but brittle: loc_raw() can hand a widget a formatted string carrying any byte, and that byte would render as a blank box. Declaring the alphabet costs a few glyphs in the atlas and removes the class. Case closure is automatic -- declare one case.

plural_rule.description: Override the CLDR rule the generator derives from the language code. Required only for a language the generator does not know.

fallback.description: The authoring language. Must be a key of `languages`, must carry text for every key, and is what shows when the active language has none.

strings.description: key -> entry. The first key segment is the surface the player sees the string on.

args.description: Declared explicitly, never inferred from the placeholder name. Every declared arg must be used by at least one form; every placeholder must be declared. Argument order fixes the generated C parameter order, so it is not reorderable without touching call sites.

plural_on.description: Names the declared argument that selects the plural form. When present, every language's value is an object of CLDR categories instead of a string. Bound to a float type, every language must carry exactly `other` -- a fractional value always selects `other`.

note.description: Free-text authoring note. Never rendered, never generated.

text.description: Player-visible text. `{name}` interpolates a declared argument; `{{` and `}}` are literal braces; `%` is literal everywhere. Newline and tab are the only control characters allowed.
